title: Clauses risk rubric & negotiation journal — NDAs/SLAs
content:
Purpose:
Quick working journal for negotiating NDAs / SLAs with a focus on inference products (model hosting, ded. capacity, private deploy). Keep this lightweight — notes to self, negotiation scripts, fallback lines, and a short risk→impact estimate for triage during fast redlines.

Top-level rubric (use this to triage clauses quickly):
- HIGH RISK: irreversible data exposure or broad IP assignment; termination without transition protections; unlimited indemnity; carve-outs that bind us to customer obligations. These need escalation and possibly legal leadership sign-off.
- MEDIUM RISK: broad usage rights over model outputs; long retention + unclear deletion obligations; subprocessors with no audit rights; SLA credits that trigger big financial exposure. Can often be handled with targeted redlines.
- LOW RISK: formatting/notice timelines, typical confidentiality definitions with mutual obligations, routine choice-of-law tweaks. Handle at rep level.

Clause-by-clause (notes + negotiation playbook):
1) Output/IP ownership (model output, embeddings):
   - Why it matters: Customers often want ownership of outputs. For hosted inference, outputs are derived using our models and infra — blanket assignment creates product risk and downstream licensing chaos.
   - Goal: Customer has a license to use results; we keep underlying model weights, system prompts, and derived improvements. Add limited rights for embeddings/outputs if they pay higher tier or dedicated.
   - Fallback language to propose: "Customer receives a non-exclusive, perpetual (or term-limited), non-transferable license to use outputs for Customer's internal business purposes; Redwood retains rights in models, underlying data, and improvements."
   - Quick script: "Happy to grant usage rights to outputs for your stated use-cases. We can’t assign model IP or derivative training rights — can we scope to ‘right to use for Product X’ instead?"
   - Impact estimate: HIGH if agreed to assignment; MID otherwise.

2) Data residency & export controls:
   - Why: Regulated customers will insist on residency and export restrictions. For Private and Dedicated, we can often comply; hosted requires region guarantees.
   - Goal: Agree on region(s) + allow for narrow exceptions for backups/DR with notice.
   - Redline suggest: Explicitly list permitted regions and require customer's prior written approval for any cross-border transfer. Add exception for legal compulsion with notice.
   - Unresolved Q: exact S3/GCP bucket naming and retention for logs — ops input needed (TODO ping infra/ops).

3) Security standards & audits:
   - Why: Customers want SOC2/ISO evidence and auditability. We should push for summary reports vs on-site audits.
   - Goal: Allow security questionnaire / SOC2 report under NDA; resist intrusive operational access or live production audits.
   - Fallback: Offer annual SOC2 Type 2 report and a security questionnaire; allow on-site only for enterprise pilot with scoped controls and expense reimbursement.

4) Indemnity & liability caps:
   - Why: Unlimited indemnities or carve-outs defeat predictable exposure. We need reciprocal indemnities and a cap tied to fees (standard = 12 months of fees or negotiated silly number).
   - Goal: Mutual indemnity for IP claims; limit liability for data incidents to a negotiated cap; carve out gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
   - Quick script: "We can take IP indemnity with standard carve-outs and a liability cap reflective of the contract value. Unlimited liability isn't something we can accept — can we align on 12 months of fees?"

5) Termination & transition / data return:
   - Why: Customers expect data export and a smooth transition; we must ensure no exposure and reasonable migration assistance.
   - Goal: Define export format, retention window, and assistance hours. For Hosted: limit export to data customer provided and outputs; for Dedicated/Private: include host support.
   - Suggested line: "On termination, Redwood will provide a copy of Customer Data in a commonly used format within 30 days and assist with migration for up to X hours at the standard hourly rate."

6) Subprocessors & supply chain:
   - Why: Use of cloud/GPU vendors, telemetry providers, etc. Customers want transparency and sometimes veto rights.
   - Goal: Provide a list of subprocessors and a mechanism to remove/change with notice; resist blanket veto rights that break our infra.
   - Tactic: Quarterly published list + 30-day notice; specific vendor removal only for material breach.

7) SLA credits & service levels:
   - Why: SLAs for latency/availability in inference are tricky — we expose SLOs, not strict contractual unlimited penalties. Credits should be a limited remedy.
   - Goal: Cap remedies to service credits; exclude third-party outages and planned maintenance. Provide clear measurement method (percent of successful requests by region, sample window).
   - Suggested negotiation point: define measurement, define credit table, and cap at X% monthly fees.

Rapid redline checklist before sending to counterparty:
- Have ops confirm retention and backup exception wording.
- Confirm we can support the listed regions (infra/regions owners).
- Get product sign-off on Output/IP fallback language (Samantha).
- Ensure SOC2 report version attached.
- Validate indemnity cap with finance for exposure modeling.

Escalation triggers (call legal lead + CTO):
- Customer insists on assignment of model weights or derivative rights.
- Unlimited liability / indemnity with no cap.
- Customer requests live production access or source code escrow beyond standard library-level escrow.
- Any data export request that conflicts with existing regulatory obligations (e.g., EU DPAs).

Negotiation scripts & phrases (short):
- "We want customers to use outputs freely; assigning model IP would prevent us from evolving and supporting multiple customers. Can we give a license tailored to your product instead?"
- "We publish our SOC2 and are willing to fill out the security questionnaire — for live audits let's scope and cover costs."
- "We can include export assistance in the termination clause — let's define the format and a migration cap so both sides know expectations."

Notes-to-self / TODOs: (quick unresolved items to close before signing)
- [ ] Confirm retention/backup exceptions with infra (owner: Jonas).
- [ ] Ask finance to run exposure calc for liability cap of 12 months fees vs 24 months. (ticket: LEGAL-711).
- [ ] Draft alternative output license allowing training/derivative carve-out. (owner: Samantha).
- [ ] Clean up vendor list and add to pipeline for quarterly publication.

Quick examples of redline snippets (short):
- Counterparty: "Company hereby assigns all rights to outputs, embeddings, and derivative works to Customer."
  - Our counter: "Company grants Customer a non-exclusive license to use Outputs for Customer's internal business operations; Company retains all rights in Models and Improvements and no ownership interest is transferred."

- Counterparty: "No liability cap for data breach."
  - Our counter: "Except for liability arising from Company’s gross negligence or willful misconduct, Company’s liability shall be limited to the greater of $X or 12 months of fees paid by Customer in the 12 months preceding the claim."

Quick mental model for rapid triage:
- If clause affects product roadmap or multi-cust upgrades → escalate to product + engineering.
- If clause modifies distribution of risk in a way that affects P&L materially → involve finance.
- If clause creates obligations for specific engineering effort/time → require SOW or change order.

Closing: keep this doc as the running journal for negotiation threads where I am the primary reviewer. When we finalize a common fallback set, copy into the contracts repo as a template (see linked GH PR). Most fast wins are by tightening definitions (what is Customer Data vs Derivative) and by putting numeric caps on open-ended remedies.

Revision log (notes to self):
- 2024-11-20: initial brainstorm and rubric.
- 2024-12-05: added SLA measurement suggestions after ops sync.
- 2025-01-07: added escalation triggers and TODOs after review with Miguel.

End of doc.
